newsitem.title: ITALY: French advance unit for Albania arrives in Italy.
newsitem.headline: French advance unit for Albania arrives in Italy.

text.p: An advance unit of about 100 French troops bound for Albania arrived in the southeast Italian port of Brindisi on Friday, witnesses said.
The group docked on the French navy auxiliary ship Champlain with a mascot dog -- Chipie.
The soldiers, mainly scouts from various units, are expected to travel on by sea to the Albanian port of Durres.

France is providing a 1,000-strong contingent to a multinational force of 6,000 led by Italy that is expected to begin full-scale deployment in Albania next week to assist in a relief mission to the anarchic Balkan state.
The first advance units of Italian soldiers arrived on Friday in Durres and at the capital Tirana's airport.
The mission, dubbed Operation Alba (sunrise), is the first of its kind to be led by Italy.

"We're happy to work under Italian command because we have had a good experience working together in Bosnia, where they were under French command. We consider this a sort of exchange of courtesies," one officer on the Champlain said.
Romania, Greece, Turkey and Spain are also sending troops and Austria and Denmark are considering participation.

Some 350 French troops of the 9th Paratroop infantry division left the southern port of Toulon for Durres on Friday aboard the landing ship Orage. The remainder of the French contingent is expected to travel to Albania by ferry next week.
